level: stop-fence design slice 3: private owner-only read-only latest-rollback readiness diagnostic
componentAcceptance: verified offline on three platforms with synthetic journal/router databases and a real ledger archive
productAcceptance: diagnostic only: it changes no byte, relaxes no money rollback guard, and postActivationRollbackSupported stays false
implementation: Opens both databases read-only (query_only) and answers one question: may the LATEST new-generation data be handed back right now? Active tasks (ready/admitting/running/cancelling/waiting-budget), unknown outcomes (needs-reconciliation), retryable blocked tasks and skipped entries whose attempt provably started are blockers with bounded ids; a skipped entry is advisory only when its own attempt never started (started_ms null plus notStarted evidence).
Open holds, unsettled operations and an undelivered outbox block; nothing is ever auto-turned into success or released.

Backup binding: the ledger archive must verify, and the archive's full private export document must equal the live export of the current router database — the verifier's redacted summary deliberately omits digests, so the binding compares the private export itself; a mismatch or post-archive mutation answers BACKUP_BINDING_STALE, a missing or invalid archive MIGRATION_READINESS_BACKUP_BINDING_INVALID.
The result always carries postActivationRollbackSupported:false and moneyRollbackGuardUntouched:true; the existing sqlite-router-state rollback() guards are untouched.

platforms.rootRegression: 1850 tests, 1782 pass, 0 fail, 68 skipped, exit 0 (log: tmp/integration/rollback-readiness-root-regression.log); the suite is registered in npm test and Windows/Ubuntu CI

preservedFailures: Development findings, all reproduced and fixed: the archive refuses an output directory under the source database (the fixture now uses separate data/archive roots); the ledger verifier returns a redacted summary without digests, so the live binding was redesigned to compare the archive's full private export document; two fixture defects (a wrong placeholder count and a Windows-absolute test path) were corrected. The first Ubuntu run failed at module load because the fixture lacked the ledger-export dependency closure; the closure was uploaded and the run rerun to green.
limitations: Readiness means no blocking state was observed at diagnosis time — it is not a stop-write or activation proof and does not verify external side effects.

The binding covers the router ledger archive; the wider cross-domain capture (sessions, memory, attachments, usage) binds through the existing archive family and remains part of slice 5 orchestration.

OS isolation adapters (slice 4), recoverable commit orchestration and activation (slice 5), and any relaxation for not-started blocked/skipped entries remain open; the money rollback guard is deliberately untouched.
